the growth of the whole system depends upon the interaction of two mechanisms: a selection process which determines market shares and a sorting process which regulates the relative position of firms within sectors.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the growth of the aggregate economy is the outcome of the interaction between a sorting and a selecting mechanism, which continuously changes firms relative positions in the market.

the Fisher Principle can be applied to a multi-sectoral setting, in which sectors are not ex-ante identical, and in which the relative position of sectors in the economy is continuously reshaped by selection.

a process of selection within and between industries, which is driven by a process of learning and innovation, can account for the observed growth rates of different sectors and for a continuous structural change in the economy.
